change.author: Eunjae Lee

findings.title: Only the first branch of getBaseConditions can run
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object (lines 83-88, 125-143), and an object is always truthy. So `authConditions` is never falsy, and the `else if (filterConditions)` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches (lines 76-79) can never run. They also suggest that a filter-only result can skip authorization, which can't happen today and would be risky if it ever did. Suggest simplifying to `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;`.

findings.title: Org and team SQL is never run against the database
findings.body: This test is now the only one that runs the generated SQL against Postgres, and it only covers `scope: "user"` with an eventTypeId filter. The org and team tests (lines 278-346) only check that the `Prisma.sql` objects are structurally equal. So the new `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` / `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` array bindings (insightsBooking.ts:164, 168, 197, 201) are never shown to work: correct parameter typing, and the right rows coming back. A `$queryRaw` test for team and org scope, with one team booking and one personal booking, would cover the part of this rewrite most likely to break. The removed caching tests also leave `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` memoization (lines 83-95) untested, and that code is still there.

findings.title: Constructor type no longer requires teamId for team scope
findings.body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope. Before, the constructor took the discriminated union. Now a caller can pass `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` without a compile error. At runtime the zod parse (line 62) fails, so the service quietly returns `1=0` and shows no data instead of a type error. That fails closed, so it's safe, but the mistake moves from compile time to a silent empty result. Keep the discriminated union, or document why the looser type is needed. No caller in the repository needs it today: the only constructor calls are in the integration test.

contracts.action: Replace findMany (Prisma where-input) with getBaseConditions returning a Prisma.Sql fragment for raw queries
contracts.equivalent_path: Old findMany AND-ed [authConditions, filterConditions] into the where clause. The sibling InsightsRoutingService.findMany still uses object where-inputs.
contracts.before_after: Before: where = { ...args.where, AND: [auth, filter?] }. After: `(auth) AND (filter)` or just `auth`. Auth is always non-null, so authorization is always applied. User scope: userId = X AND teamId IS NULL, same as before. Team and org scope: the same OR of team bookings and member personal bookings. The team branch now leaves out the userId clause when the member list is empty; before it was `in: []`, which matched nothing, so results are the same.
contracts.visible_effect: There are no production callers in the repository yet (grep finds only the integration test). The fragment is meant to be put into $queryRaw WHERE clauses for insights pages.
contracts.failure_mode: Invalid options or a non-admin user give `1=0`, so no rows: fails closed. DB errors from the TeamRepository/MembershipRepository lookups reject getBaseConditions and reach the caller. Nothing is cached when a call rejects, because the cache field stays undefined.

summary:
I found no bugs in this PR, only three "consider" items. It moves the booking insights service from Prisma where-objects to `Prisma.sql` fragments that get dropped into raw queries. I compared the new conditions with the old ones for user, team and org scope and for both filters. They return the same rows, and authorization is always applied: invalid options or a non-admin user still get `1=0`, so no rows. The three items:
- **Unreachable branches (cleanup):** `getBaseConditions` has fallback branches that can never run, because the authorization fragment is always present.
- **Test coverage:** only the user-scope query is run against the database, so the new `= ANY(array)` conditions for team and org scope are only checked structurally. The deleted caching tests also leave the caching code, which is still there, untested.
- **Looser constructor type:** the new options type no longer forces `teamId` for team scope. A missing `teamId` now shows up as an empty result instead of a type error.
